answer: Each identity earns weight only through one registered excavation permit for a site: one dig season, daily logs countersigned by the director, and all finds catalogued in the museum registry, including cedar beams dated by ring analysis. Each fake costs one season: 90 field days plus a 1,400-unit fee, so 100 fakes cost 140,000 units and 9,000 days; on a tundra site, frozen ground limits digging to 60 days. A copied catalogue fails because every find is photographed against the site grid, so a crystal bead with no photo exposes the cluster, and one operator cannot run two digs at once.
